regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like a vintage year — until you note that the RBI's own forecast sits 110bps lower at 6.7% YoY, and core sector growth decelerated to 4.8% YoY even as IIP capital goods accelerated to 16.9% YoY. The divergence between infrastructure-linked output and broader industrial momentum is the tell: this is a government-capex-led cycle, not a broad-based private recovery. PMI Composite at 55.9 is real, but passenger vehicle sales falling for two consecutive months to 7.9% YoY and commercial vehicle sales sliding to 12.6% YoY suggest the consumption underbelly is softer than the headline.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 5.54% YoY is 44bps above RBI's upper tolerance band, but the composition is what should unsettle the MPC: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, the highest in the dataset) is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, which will migrate into core goods prices with a 2-3 quarter lag. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY looks contained — but that is precisely the trap. If Brent holds above $105/bbl, the fuel-to-core transmission will push headline CPI toward 6.5% by Q1 FY28, forcing RBI to hike into a slowing consumption cycle. The RBI's own inflation forecast has already moved up 50bps to 5.1% YoY — the direction of travel is unambiguous.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY growing for three consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4%) while deposits grew 17.8% YoY — a 160bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81%, the 73rd percentile historically. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% during a rate-cut cycle was Q2 FY14; within 12 months the taper tantrum forced 75bps of emergency hikes and deposit rate wars compressed NIMs by 40-60bps across mid-sized banks. The setup today is structurally similar, except NBFC credit is accelerating at 15.8% YoY and corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month signals wholesale funding dependency rising — not falling. The regulator's next move is risk weights, not rate cuts.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on extended pause, but the real rate is being compressed from below: CPI at 5.54% YoY means the ex-ante real repo rate is effectively negative 29bps. A central bank with a negative real rate, a CD ratio at the 73rd percentile, fuel inflation at the 95th percentile, and a currency at the 89th percentile of depreciation has no room to cut — and the market pricing any easing in the next two quarters is mispricing the optionality. The RBI's inflation forecast upgrade to 5.1% YoY is the clearest signal: the pause is not a pivot.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (up from 16.1% YoY) and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%) make the capex upcycle look durable — and at 77.4%, the threshold for private greenfield investment (typically 80%+) is within one quarter's reach. Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (up from 7% YoY) and credit to services at 24.3% YoY confirm that banks are funding the cycle. The inversion: core sector at 4.8% YoY decelerated even as IIP capital goods accelerated — meaning the investment is in machinery and equipment, not in cement and steel-intensive infrastructure. That is a quality upgrade, not a warning sign.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is a 73rd-percentile print, but the composition matters more than the headline: two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY (61st percentile) signal rural recovery, while passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY falling for two consecutive months and commercial vehicle sales at 12.6% YoY falling for two consecutive months signal urban discretionary and freight demand softening simultaneously. The GST number is partly a formalization story — the YoY base is clean, but the sequential trend (₹2,00,640→₹1,99,853→₹2,03,521 cr / month) shows no acceleration. Consumption is stable at the aggregate level while bifurcating sharply beneath it: rural two-wheelers recovering, urban four-wheelers and trucks fading.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4% credit; deposits 9.9→17.8%). CD ratio at 81% credit-to-deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), with corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month — alternative funding channels opening but wholesale dependency rising.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios >45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities; their cost of funds will spike if deposit growth doesn't re-accelerate. Watch for RBI to signal deposit-friendly measures (higher savings rates, CRR cuts) within 2-3 months. Tactical short on mid-cap NBFCs with <₹500 cr AUM.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile is manageable but the *trend* is the risk — credit outpacing deposits for 2 months straight is a regime shift. Last time this happened (2018-19), RBI tightened liquidity and NBFC funding seized.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadening Beyond Cyclicals","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (Mar 2026, up from 16.1% YoY), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), and core sector growth at 4.8% YoY. Manufacturing PMI at 55.1 index (up from 52.8), services PMI at 55.2 index (up from 54.1). Credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (up from 7% YoY) and credit to services at 24.3% YoY (up from 10.3% YoY) — both accelerating sharply. India GDP FY estimate at 7.7% YoY (80th percentile hi), RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% YoY (76th percentile mid).","implication":"Overweight capital goods, industrial machinery, and cement stocks — order books are filling. Rotate into services capex plays (IT infrastructure, logistics, warehousing) as credit to services is now outpacing industrial credit. Avoid defensive plays; the cycle is broadening. Tactical long on Nifty 50 with 60% weight in cyclicals, 40% in services. Monitor order book commentary in Q4 earnings — if order inflows remain >₹500 cr per company, extend positions.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at 74th percentile — historically, capex accelerates when CU crosses 75%. The last time services credit grew 24% YoY was 2021-22, which preceded a 3-year bull run in IT and logistics.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Momentum Masks Affluent Rotation","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (Mar 2026), rising 3 consecutive months (₹29,845→₹31,961→₹32,297→₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (down from 10.45 mn, but up from 9.9 mn — volatile). SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (up from ₹16.64 lakh cr over 3 months). Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (up from ₹29,329 cr / month), at 80th percentile hi. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile hi), offsetting FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month. MF average AUM at ₹87.09 lakh cr (72nd percentile, strong-positive signal).","implication":"SIP inflows are real, but the *composition* is shifting — average ticket size rising (SIP AUM +₹1.22 lakh cr while accounts fell 390k) means affluent money entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (Nifty 50 over Nifty Midcap 150). Reduce exposure to micro-cap and speculative plays. Hedge with 10-15% allocation to gold or long-duration bonds — affluent SIP rotation often precedes a 15-20% correction.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile hi; last time they were this high (2021), the market peaked 6 months later. The divergence between account growth (slowing) and AUM growth (accelerating) is a classic late-cycle signal.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (Mar 2026, up from 20.05% YoY) — at 95th percentile hi, the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at $109.69 / bbl (flat, but up from $103.4 / bbl 3 months ago). WTI at $99.04 / bbl (up from $90.61 / bbl 3 months ago). FAO food index at 136 index (up from 134.5 index), with food inflation at 7.74% YoY (up from 5.97% YoY, rising 2 consecutive months). India's headline CPI at 5.54% YoY (up from 4.83% YoY), driven by fuel and food. RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6% YoY).","implication":"Reduce exposure to discretionary consumption (auto, retail, FMCG) — margin compression is imminent as input costs rise faster than pricing power. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) and fertiliser plays (which benefit from commodity tailwinds). Hedge with long positions in Brent futures or energy ETFs. Monitor RBI's next policy meeting (likely May 2026) — if fuel inflation stays >20%, expect a 25 bps rate hike, which will pressure growth stocks. Avoid airlines and logistics stocks with unhedged fuel exposure.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a regime signal — last time it was this high (2022), RBI hiked rates 190 bps in 6 months and growth stocks fell 35%. The current 22.93% is unsustainable and will force policy tightening.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"BOJ Tightening Unwinds Carry Trade Flows","data_text":"BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1% p.a., rising 2 consecutive months) — at 100th percentile hi, the highest in the dataset. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a., rising 2 in a row), at 68th percentile mid. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (up from 2.25% p.a., rising 2 in a row). US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.1% (down from 5.19%, but still at 92nd percentile hi). US PMI composite at 58.4 index (up from 56, at 91st percentile hi), signalling strong US growth. Global PMI composite at 54.3 index (up from 53.5, at 84th percentile hi). DXY at 101.779 index (flat, at 54th percentile mid).","implication":"BOJ tightening is the tail risk — carry trades funded in JPY are unwinding, which will pressure EM currencies and equities. INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (up from 94.95, strong-negative signal at -78 score) is already weakening. Reduce leverage in India equities; the carry trade unwind could trigger a 5-8% correction. Overweight USD-denominated assets and reduce INR exposure. Watch for BOJ guidance in May 2026 — if they signal further hikes, expect a 10-15% EM equity selloff. Hedge with long USD positions or short JPY carry trades.","pct_10y":100,"pct_note":"BOJ at 100th percentile hi is a structural shift — for 15 years, BOJ was the world's liquidity provider. Now it's tightening, which historically precedes EM crises. The last time BOJ hiked aggressively (2000), EM equities fell 40% in 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Signals RBI Intervention Limits","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹ / USD (up from 94.95 ₹ / USD, strong-negative signal at -78 score, 89th percentile hi). FII equity net outflows at ₹49,935 cr / month (mild-negative signal at -33 score, 17th percentile lo). DII equity net inflows at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile hi), barely offsetting FII outflows. India VIX at 14.025 index (flat, at 9th percentile lo — complacency). US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.1% (92nd percentile hi), widening the India-US yield differential. Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (68th percentile mid), creating carry incentives against INR.","implication":"INR weakness is structural, not cyclical — RBI's intervention capacity is finite, and FII outflows are accelerating. Expect INR to test 96.50 ₹ / USD within 2 months. Reduce INR exposure; hedge with USD forwards or long USD calls. Avoid rupee-denominated debt; prefer USD-denominated bonds or gold. Monitor RBI's FX reserve adequacy — if reserves fall below $600 bn, expect a 50 bps rate hike to defend the currency. Tactical short on INR via NDF or currency futures. Overweight exporters (IT, pharma, auto) who benefit from INR weakness.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile hi (weak) is a regime signal — last time INR was this weak (2022), it fell another 8% before RBI intervened. The current FII outflow pattern mirrors 2022, suggesting further weakness ahead.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter, but strong-negative signal at -86 score, 7th percentile lo). Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (up from 13.74%, neutral signal). Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (down from 7.5%, strong-positive signal at 84 score, 8th percentile lo). Nifty IT index flat YTD while office absorption is collapsing — a 180-degree divergence. Bank credit to services at 24.3% YoY (up from 10.3% YoY), but NOT flowing to traditional IT office space. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹109 / sqft / mo (up from ₹100 / sqft / mo), but absorption falling — a classic supply-demand disconnect.","implication":"The IT services office narrative is broken. GCCs (Global Capability Centres) are the real buyer, not traditional IT services firms. They're consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (hence flat absorption despite rising rents). This means: (1) Avoid commercial RE plays betting on IT office demand — they're oversupplied. (2) Overweight retail mall REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) — retail vacancy is collapsing while office is stuck. (3) Reduce IT services exposure; the office-as-a-proxy for IT growth is dead. (4) Watch for GCC announcements from MNCs — they're the real demand driver, not Infosys or TCS capex. Tactical short on office-heavy REITs; long on retail-focused REITs.","pct_10y":7,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 7th percentile lo is a structural break — for 10 years, office absorption tracked IT services growth. Now it's decoupling. Retail vacancy at 8th percentile lo (tight) is the opposite signal, suggesting a bifurcated real estate market where retail thrives while office stagnates.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline — Two-Wheeler Recovery vs Four-Wheeler Fade

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile) — but RBI's own forecast is 6.7% YoY, a 110bps gap that reflects the statistical discrepancy between headline output and ground-level demand.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural recovery; but passenger vehicle sales fell for two consecutive months to 7.9% YoY and commercial vehicle sales to 12.6% YoY — urban and freight demand softening together.
  • PMI Composite at 55.9 index (85th percentile) with manufacturing at 55.1 and services at 55.2 — both accelerating — confirms the activity pulse is real.
  • But core sector growth decelerated to 4.8% YoY even as IIP capital goods hit 16.9% YoY — investment in machinery is outrunning infrastructure throughput.

The tension: The headline GDP and PMI signal a broad expansion; the vehicle sales decomposition and core sector deceleration signal a narrower, investment-led cycle with consumption bifurcating along the rural-urban axis.

Bottom line: Watch two-wheeler sales for rural demand confirmation — a third consecutive month above 25% YoY would validate the consumption broadening thesis; a reversal would not.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US PMI at 91st Percentile — Growth Signal, Tightening Consequence

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite at 58.4 index (91st percentile, rising two consecutive months) and Global PMI Composite at 54.3 index (84th percentile) — the strongest synchronised DM growth signal since 2021.
  • But US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR (50th percentile) lags the PMI optimism; US CPI at 3.72% YoY rising three consecutive months means the Fed has no permission to cut.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, rising two consecutive months) — the highest rate in the dataset — is unwinding the yen carry trade that funded EM inflows for three years.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.1% yield (92nd percentile) — down from 5.19% but structurally elevated — keeps the India-US yield differential compressed and EM carry unattractive.

The tension: DM PMIs are pricing re-acceleration; DM central banks are still tightening or holding at cycle highs. The bond market is not giving equities the rate relief they are pricing.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underappreciated tail — a further 25bps hike would trigger yen carry unwind and EM liquidity withdrawal within 60 days.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Masks NFO Collapse — Smart Money Pausing

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising three consecutive months — the structural retail bid is intact and absorbing market volatility.
  • But NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile, down from ₹3,051 cr / month) — the lowest in the dataset — signal that fund houses are not launching because they cannot deploy capital at current valuations.
  • DII equity net inflows at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) are barely offsetting FII equity net outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) — a ₹1,894 cr / month net margin.
  • MF Average AUM at ₹87.09 lakh cr (86th percentile) — down from ₹88.31 lakh cr — reflects mark-to-market pressure despite inflow momentum.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are structurally resilient; institutional and fund-house behaviour (NFO freeze, FII exit) signals that the marginal buyer at current prices is the least informed one.

Bottom line: If FII outflows sustain above ₹40,000 cr / month for a second consecutive month, DII absorption will require SIP acceleration that the 10.7% YoY SIP growth rate cannot guarantee.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Bid Holds Premium Segment — REIT Prices Contradict Office Rents

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 10%, +10 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $73 bn (12.8% YoY) provide the funding base.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum at 15% YoY sales growth with launches up 120% YoY — but 28 months of unsold inventory is the trapdoor beneath the headline.
  • Bengaluru office absorption at 5.2 mn sq ft / quarter (11% YoY) with rents at ₹109/sqft/mo — but Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit is down from ₹435, Mindspace at ₹345/unit down from ₹495.
  • Bank Nifty at 55,844 (92nd percentile) — flat on the session — while credit-deposit stress at 81% CD ratio should be compressing NIM expectations, not expanding them.

The tension: Office rents are rising and GCC demand (41% of occupier mix) is structurally sound, but REIT unit prices have fallen 15-30% — the market is pricing a vacancy risk that the rent data does not yet confirm.

Bottom line: REITs are a buy only if office vacancy stabilises below 14% — watch the next quarterly absorption print; above 14.5% vacant triggers further REIT derating.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Four Risks, One Trigger — Crude Holds the Key

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $109.69/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15 bn to India's import bill, widens CAD by ~40bps, and pushes CPI toward 6.5% YoY by Q1 FY28.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — a further 25bps hike unwinds yen carry, accelerates FII outflows beyond ₹49,935 cr / month, and tests RBI's FX intervention capacity.
  • CD ratio at 81% (73rd percentile) with credit growing at 19.4% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, NBFC funding costs rise and the bear scenario (credit crunch cascade) activates.
  • INR at 95.24 ₹/USD (89th percentile) with India VIX at 14.025 (9th percentile) — complacency in volatility pricing while currency stress is at a near-decade high is a classic pre-dislocation setup.

The tension: All four risks share a common accelerant: a Brent print above $115/bbl would simultaneously worsen CAD, force RBI to defend INR, tighten domestic liquidity, and compress corporate margins — the bear scenario needs only one catalyst.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week — a close above $112/bbl shifts the base scenario to bear and makes an RBI emergency communication (not a cut) the most likely policy response.

"}
